title: Chann CRM AI agent-test scenario
description: One test case, written as data. The runner (scripts/agent-test/run.py) enforces this contract itself before executing anything, so a scenario that runs is a scenario every key of which was understood; this file is the same contract in a form other tools can read. YAML files are validated against it after being parsed.

name.description: Unique, lowercase, dashes only. This is what --only matches on.

description.description: One line saying what journey this covers; shown by --list.

backend.description: fake = the in-memory Data client, no database. db = the real Data tier over HTTP against TEST_DATABASE_URL. any = runs on either; the runner skips a scenario whose backend does not match the one selected.

oa.description: Which LINE Official Account the message arrives on. This, not the role, decides what the OA is allowed to offer.

role.description: The identity's primary role (sales, technician, owner, cs...). Defaults to technician on the technician OA, sales otherwise.

permissions.description: fake backend only; on the db backend the member's real role decides and this is reported as ignored.

line_user_id.description: db backend only. Omit unless a scenario needs a SECOND person: the default is one LINE account shared by every OA, which is what migration 0026 is about.

oneOf.description: A named set. sales/technician/customer are the sets the three OAs normally carry.

step.description: Exactly one of send / seed / reset / http, optionally with `expect`; or a bare `expect` that asserts on the last reply.

note.description: A comment carried into the JSON report. Does nothing.

reset.description: Fresh state: a new fake client, or a new tenant on the db backend. Any value; `true` reads best.

send.description: A chat message. A plain string is the message with every actor default; a mapping overrides them for this message only.

ai.description: What the language model would have answered, had it been called. Supplied because no scenario may reach a real model. Omit and the model answers 'suggest', which is how you prove a message is handled deterministically (see used_ai).

seed.description: Shop data the scenario needs, created through the same data client the run is using — so the tier's own validation applies. Every row may carry `ref: <name>`, which makes it referable later as "$name" (its id) or "$name.field".

members.description: fake backend only — a membership row invented directly. On the db backend a member is made by redeeming an invite.

redeem.description: db backend only. Each row: {invite: "$ref.invite_code", oa: technician|sales, line_user_id?, display_name?}. Omitting line_user_id means the scenario's own LINE account redeems it, which is the migration-0026 case.

raw.description: fake backend only. Writes rows straight onto the fake client's private state (`tickets` sets _tickets, and so on). The escape hatch for a starting state no client call can produce, such as a ticket already assigned and awaiting acceptance.

call.description: Anything the shorthands do not cover: {method: <data client method>, args: {...}, ref?: <name>}. The licence id is passed as the first argument for you.

http.description: db backend only: call an Application-tier route the dashboard uses. `{license_id}` in the path is filled in.

as.description: Who is calling. Defaults to the shop owner with every permission.

expect.description: Assertions on the step's result — the reply of a `send`, the response of an `http`, or the last of either for a bare expect. All of them must hold; all of them are reported, not just the first that fails.

contains.description: Every one of these must appear in the reply text.

not_contains.description: None of these may appear. Use it to keep raw field names (due_time, service_address) and other OAs' vocabulary out of a reply.

quick_replies_include.description: Matches a quick-reply button's label or the text it sends.

has_image.description: Whether the reply carries image URLs (guides that need a picture do).

intent.description: The parsed intent the reply carried. Only replies routed through the model carry one.

max_lines.description: LINE readability: a bubble longer than about 15 lines is not read.

is_not.description: The reply must not be one of the known failure shapes.

used_ai.description: false asserts the answer came from the deterministic layer without calling the model at all.

status.description: http steps only: the HTTP status code.

json_path.description: http steps only: dotted path -> expected value, compared as strings. Digits index into arrays, e.g. "0.channel".

json_contains.description: http steps only: the serialised response body must contain each string.

badClass.description: not_sure = 'I am not sure what you want'. permission = a refusal for lack of a permission key. not_found = nothing matched. generic_error = a bare apology. not_a_feature = 'the system does not do that'. ai_down = the model was unreachable.
